## Sedimentation of condensates (`sedimentation`) {#sec-ch10-sed}

Condensate particles fall through the gas at their terminal velocity. snapy adds that motion as an extra $x_1$ flux
of the condensate's mass, the momentum it carries and its energy, on top of the advective flux the Riemann solver
returns. The velocity is the slip-corrected Stokes velocity of a sphere in the background gas, or a prescribed
constant. The flux is donor-cell, sealed at physical $x_1$ walls and open at internal block seams. Dry air does not
move, so the dry-air tracers of @sec-ch10-tracer are unaffected.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Lets each listed condensate settle at a terminal velocity, as a donor-cell $x_1$ flux; @eq-ch10-sed-stokes.

**Data.** Reads the cell primitives and each condensate's radius and density; adds to the $x_1$ face fluxes `flux1`.

**Placement.** Every RK stage, after the $x_1$ Riemann solve and before the seam average.

**Activation.** Top-level YAML `sedimentation` (off when absent); requires `forcing/const-gravity`.

**Guarantee / limits.** First order in space; sealed at physical $x_1$ walls, open at seams; no time-step bound.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch10-sed-tests; `test_sedimentation_guards.release`, `test_forcing.release`, `sed_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C8]`.
:::

Local symbols: $a_n$ is the particle radius of condensate $n$ [m], $\rho_{\mathrm p,n}$ its material density
[$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$], $\beta_n$ the Cunningham slip factor [-], $\lambda$ the mean free path of the background gas
[m], $\mathrm{Kn}=\lambda/a_n$ the Knudsen number [-], and $m_{\mathrm{mol}}$, $d_{\mathrm{mol}}$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{LJ}}$ the
molecular mass [kg], molecular diameter [m] and Lennard-Jones well depth [J] of the background gas (YAML `a-mass`,
`a-diameter`, `a-epsilon-LJ`); $k_{\mathrm B}$ is Boltzmann's constant, as in @sec-ch02, and $\mu$[^rg-e36e3b696e97] the dynamic viscosity
of appendix A, notation group 8. Bare $m$ is the momentum, bare $d$ is not used, and bare $\epsilon$ is the pivot tolerance, so all
three carry a subscript here.

**How to use it.** A top-level `sedimentation` block lists cloud species by name, and the card needs constant gravity
({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_options.cpp SedVelOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}};
{{< code examples/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.yaml >}}):

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `forcing`[^rg-41e2c46cc4d2], `const-gravity`[^rg-7342e035beb2], `grav1`[^rg-20d0270c17e8], `radius`[^rg-7b9938338dec], `density`[^rg-4e0de53e039d], `const-vsed`[^rg-e24cc2e272ce].
```yaml
forcing:
  const-gravity: {grav1: -22.}
sedimentation:
  radius:  {"H2O(l,p)": 1.0e-10}     # a_n [m]; quote the name: YAML splits an unquoted key at the comma
  density: {"H2O(l,p)": 1000.}       # rho_p,n [kg m^-3]
  const-vsed: {"H2O(l,p)": -1.0}     # optional: replaces eq-ch10-sed-stokes, still clamped
  # a-diameter, a-epsilon-LJ, a-mass, upper-limit: H2 defaults 2.827e-10, 8.24e-22, 3.34e-27, 5e3
```

The refusals are listed in the Code layer below.

### Derivation

Why the terminal velocity has this form:

1. *Stokes drag.* A sphere of radius $a_n$ moving slowly at velocity $w$ through a gas of viscosity $\mu$ feels
   $6\pi\mu a_nw$.
2. *Balance.* Setting it equal to the buoyant weight $\tfrac43\pi a_n^3(\rho_{\mathrm p,n}-\rho)g_1$ gives
   $w=2a_n^2g_1(\rho_{\mathrm p,n}-\rho)/(9\mu)$ (`[C6]`, sympy).
3. *Slip.* When the mean free path is not small compared with the particle, the drag is reduced by the Cunningham
   factor $\beta_n=1+\mathrm{Kn}\,(1.256+0.4\,e^{-1.1/\mathrm{Kn}})$, which tends to 1 in the continuum and to
   $1.656\,\mathrm{Kn}$ in the free-molecular limit (`[C2]`, `[C8]`).
4. *Hence*, unless a non-zero `const-vsed` replaces it,

$$
w_{\mathrm{s},n} = \frac{2\beta_n\,a_n^2\,g_1\,(\rho_{\mathrm{p},n}-\rho)}{9\,\mu}.
$$ {#eq-ch10-sed-stokes}

@eq-ch10-sed-stokes is computed in `SedVelImpl::forward` as `stokes`
({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_vel.cpp SedVelImpl::forward >}}). A non-zero `const_vsed` replaces it, and either
value is then clamped to $\pm$`upper-limit`.
The viscosity is the Chapman-Enskog value for a Lennard-Jones gas,

$$
\mu = \frac{5}{16}\,\frac{\sqrt{m_{\mathrm{mol}}\,k_{\mathrm B}T/\pi}\,(k_{\mathrm B}T/\epsilon_{\mathrm{LJ}})^{0.16}}{1.22\,d_{\mathrm{mol}}^2}.
$$ {#eq-ch10-sed-viscosity}

This is the Chapman-Enskog viscosity $\mu=\tfrac5{16}\sqrt{\pi m_{\mathrm{mol}}k_{\mathrm B}T}\big/\big(\pi d_{\mathrm{mol}}^2\,\Omega_{\mathrm{c}}\big)$
with the collision integral approximated as $\Omega_{\mathrm{c}}=1.22\,(k_{\mathrm B}T/\epsilon_{\mathrm{LJ}})^{-0.16}$ (local
symbol; $\Omega$[^rg-51287c24f565] alone is the rotation rate),
with molecular mass $m_{\mathrm{mol}}$,
diameter $d_{\mathrm{mol}}$ and well depth $\epsilon_{\mathrm{LJ}}$ from the YAML defaults of an $\mathrm{H_2}$ background, and the mean free path
is $\lambda=(\mu/p)\sqrt{\pi k_{\mathrm B}T/(2m_{\mathrm{mol}})}$; the code calls $\mu$ `eta`
({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_vel.cpp SedVelImpl::forward >}}).
The port confirms the sign convention ($g_1<0$ and a dense particle settle, `[C1]`), the two limits of
$\beta_n$ (1 in the continuum, $1.656\,\mathrm{Kn}$ in the free-molecular limit, `[C2]`), that $\mu$ depends on $T$
only (`[C3]`), the clamp and the prescribed velocity (`[C4]`), and the Chapman-Enskog form against the code's `eta`
(`[C7]`).[^sed-c]

The flux through the face below cell $i$ takes its donor from cell $i$ when $w_{\mathrm s,n}<0$ and from cell $i-1$
when $w_{\mathrm s,n}>0$; faces at or beyond a physical $x_1$ wall carry nothing, `sedimentation_upwind`
({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro_dispatch.hpp sedimentation_upwind >}}).
The donor carries $\rho_nw_{\mathrm s,n}$ of mass, $\mathbf v\,\rho_nw_{\mathrm s,n}$ of momentum and
$\rho_nw_{\mathrm s,n}\big(u^{\star}_n+c_{v,n}T+\tfrac12\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2\big)$ of energy: the condensate's own
specific internal energy plus specific kinetic energy, with no $R_nT$ share, because a condensate does no pressure work,
`species_energy` ({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro_impl.h sedimentation_donor_impl >}}).
With both walls sealed the column's condensate mass changes only by what the advective flux does (`[C5]`).

[^sed-c]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch10/checks/sed_check.py`, output `sed_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C8]`; a numpy port
    of `SedVelImpl::forward` and `sedimentation_upwind` at the pin with the Boltzmann constant of kintera at
    `c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77`, double precision.
    Run on CPU, one process, with Python 3.12.10, sympy 1.14.0 and numpy 2.5.3; the output matches the committed file.

### Numerical method

The flux is added to `flux1` after the $x_1$ Riemann solve and before the $x_1$ seam faces are made single-valued.
With species present and either the limiter or the face-flux covariance switch on (the switch is on by default),
its condensate part is saved as `fsed1`, so the positivity limiter can carry the right energy and momentum with it
and keeps a cell the settling flux drains out of the relaxation of @eq-ch08-theta-relax
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}; @sec-ch08-carry).
With the ideal-moist EOS and contiguous tensors a fused CPU or CUDA kernel computes velocity and flux in one pass;
otherwise a tensor path does the same in separate operations
({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro.cpp SedHydroImpl::forward >}}). MPS[^rg-7722eb7d31ba] has its own kernel,
`sedimentation_flux_mps`, behind the same dispatch stub
({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro_dispatch.cpp sedimentation_flux_mps >}}).
The wall bounds are set only where the block face is a physical boundary, so seams between blocks stay open.
@fig-ch10-sed-donor shows a column; @fig-ch10-sed-vsed the velocity.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| YAML keys | {{< code src/sedimentation/sed_options.cpp SedVelOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `check_keys` | `sedimentation` |
| terminal velocity | {{< code src/sedimentation/sed_vel.cpp SedVelImpl::forward >}} | `SedVelImpl::forward` | `const-vsed` |
| gravity required | {{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro.cpp SedHydroImpl::reset >}} | `SedHydroImpl::reset` | `const-gravity` |
| face kernel | {{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro_impl.h sedimentation_flux_impl >}} | `sedimentation_flux_impl` | |
| call site | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `fsed1` | |

: Code map of sedimentation. {#tbl-ch10-sed-code}

1. Parse the block and require cloud species ({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_options.cpp SedHydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. Read the gas constants and the clamp `upper_limit`, with their defaults
   ({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_options.cpp SedVelOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
3. Refuse a card without constant gravity, `grav` ({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro.cpp SedHydroImpl::reset >}}).
4. Skip when $g_1=0$ or nothing settles, seal physical walls, `is_physical_boundary`
   ({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro.cpp SedHydroImpl::forward >}}).
5. Choose the fused or the tensor path, `sedimentation_flux_tensor`
   ({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro.cpp SedHydroImpl::forward >}}).
6. Add to `flux1` and save the condensate part, `psed` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

Refused at setup, each with its message:

1. A key outside `radius`, `density`, `const-vsed`, `a-diameter`, `a-epsilon-LJ`, `a-mass`, `upper-limit`
   ("unknown key 'sedimentation/…'").
2. A name that is not a species ("Sedimentation particle '…' is not a valid species.").
3. A species that is not a cloud ("Missing sedimentation particles in the clouds.").
4. A non-positive radius or density ("Sedimentation radius must be positive.", "Sedimentation density must be
   positive.").
5. A particle with neither a radius nor a non-zero `const-vsed` ("Sedimentation particle '…' needs radius > 0 or a
   non-zero const-vsed."), because the velocity would be undefined.
6. A card without constant gravity ("[SedHydro] sedimentation reads grav1; set forcing/const-gravity"), because
   @eq-ch10-sed-stokes needs $g_1$[^rg-15271d05a269].

The velocity of @eq-ch10-sed-stokes is these lines ({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_vel.cpp SedVelImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
  auto eta = (5.0 / 16.0) * std::sqrt(m * KBoltz / M_PI) * torch::sqrt(temp) *
             torch::pow(reduced_temp, 0.16) / (d * d * 1.22);
  ...
  auto beta = 1.0 + Kn * (1.256 + 0.4 * torch::exp(-1.1 / Kn));
  ...
  auto stokes =
      beta / (9.0 * eta) *
      (2.0 * sqr(radius.view(vec)) * grav * (density.view(vec) - dens));
  ...
  auto vel = torch::where(cvsed != 0.0, cvsed, stokes);
  return vel.clamp(-options->upper_limit(), options->upper_limit());
```

`eta` is @eq-ch10-sed-viscosity, `beta` the Cunningham factor of step 3, `stokes` @eq-ch10-sed-stokes, and the last two
lines the prescribed velocity and the clamp.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_forcing.release` | fused equals tensor path; sealing | $10^{-10}$ rel.; exact | test thresholds |
| `test_sedimentation_guards.release` | gravity required; rising from below | $10^{-9}$ rel. | test threshold |
| `test_sedimentation_cubed_seam.release` | 2-rank seam, mass conserved; the momentum and energy sums of the mixed seam flux equal 99901.855127834307 and 499161.89154918579 | $10^{-12}$ rel.; $10^{-7}$ and $5\times10^{-3}$ abs. | test thresholds |
| `test_two_cards_species.release` | velocity after a second card | $10^{-10}$ (f64) | test threshold |

: Tests of sedimentation; the run of @tbl-ch10-ctest-run is recorded at the sha in its footnote. {#tbl-ch10-sed-tests}

The fused kernel must equal the tensor path to $10^{-10}$ relative and settle (negative flux) inside the column
({{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.fused_sedimentation_matches_tensor_path >}}).
**Total energy with sedimentation.** With the default `gravity-work: face` the settling mass flux enters the face
gravity work, so a column's total energy $E+\rho\Phi$ changes only by its boundary fluxes. One step of a settling
column holds this to $10^{-9}$ absolute
({{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.vertical_gravity_work_includes_sedimentation_mass_flux >}}).
**Not provided:** the same check for the other gravity-work forms or over a whole run; no registered test does it.
A rising cloud must be taken from the cell below, mass and energy fluxes to $10^{-9}$ relative, on CPU and CUDA
({{< code tests/test_sedimentation_guards.cpp expect_rising_cloud_taken_from_below >}}).
On two ranks of a cubed sphere, the condensate mass is conserved to $10^{-12}$ relative and two seam sums are pinned
to $10^{-7}$ and $5\times10^{-3}$ absolute
({{< code tests/test_sedimentation_cubed_seam.cpp main >}}). The sums are those of a mixed cloud flux, advected up
and settling down, so they lock the two donors of the carry (@sec-ch08-carry). The vapour there has one ratio
everywhere over over-drained dry air, so the relaxation of @eq-ch08-theta-relax withholds none of it, and the pinned
values are those of that rule, as the test's comment states;
the Gloo arm `test_sedimentation_cubed_seam_gloo` must reproduce the UCX[^rg-b90e03039e3e] result. Every ctest named here that the CPU build registers passed in the run of @tbl-ch10-ctest-run, at the sha its
footnote records; the CUDA and Gloo arms are not registered in that build and were not run. At the pin,
`test_sedimentation_cubed_seam.release` pins the values above and has not been run for this report (missing
evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The time step has no sedimentation term: `HydroImpl::max_time_step` does not read $w_{\mathrm s,n}$, so a fast
settling speed can over-drain a cell, and only the positivity limiter catches it.
:::

- The MPS path is untested: no registered test runs on MPS.
- libtorch's `Module::to` casts every buffer, so casting a block to float32 also casts the index buffer
  `hydro_ids`. The fused path converts it back to int64 before use
  ({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro.cpp SedHydroImpl::forward >}}); the tensor path indexes with it as it is
  ({{< code src/sedimentation/sed_hydro.cpp sedimentation_flux_tensor >}}). A float32 block on the tensor path is
  not tested.
- There is no frictional heating key: `forcing` refuses `fric-heat`, because the $x_1$ face gravity work already
  carries the sedimentation part of the mass flux (@sec-ch09-framework, @sec-ch06).
- The default gas constants describe $\mathrm{H_2}$; other backgrounds must set them.
- Not in the switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix).
